examples.en: I learn sign language every weekend.
Sign language communicates with hands and facial expressions.

examples.ko: 뉴스 화면 한쪽에서 수화 통역을 해 줘요.
examples.en: Sign language interpretation is shown on one side of the news screen.
That friend talks in sign language.
I want to join a sign language club.
The sign language teacher showed it slowly.

explain: '수화'는 손 모양과 움직임으로 말하는 언어예요. 요즘은 '수어'라는 말을 더 많이 권장하고, 한국어의 소리와 다른 독립된 언어라는 뜻을 담아요. 둘 다 쓰이니 뉴스나 학교에서는 '한국 수어'도 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: My friend greeted me in sign language.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수화'와 같은 뜻이고 요즘 더 권장하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수화, and the term now more recommended.

phrases.en: That person talks in sign language.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 방법으로 말하는지 '-로'로 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -로 to show the way of speaking.

phrases.en: There is sign language interpretation at the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말을 수화로 바꿔 주는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to turning speech into sign language.

explain_en: Older, common term; signing as seen in news interpretation. 수화 is a language spoken with hand shapes and movements. These days 수어 is more often recommended, stressing that it is a language separate from spoken Korean. Both are used, so also learn 한국 수어, which you will see in news and schools.

t90.ax: That friend talks in sign language.

en: to be published; to be printed

examples.ko: 제 첫 번째 책이 다음 달에 출판돼요.
examples.en: My first book will be published next month.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 십 년 전에 출판되었어요.
examples.en: This novel was published ten years ago.

examples.ko: 출판된 책은 서점에서 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: A published book can be bought at a bookstore.
That poetry collection was also published in English.
It took a year before the manuscript got published.
It became a bestseller as soon as it was published.

explain: '나오다'가 말할 때 더 자연스러워서 '책이 나왔어요'라고 많이 해요. '출판되다'는 책, 잡지 같은 인쇄물에 써요. 인터넷에 올리는 글은 '게시되다', '올라오다'가 맞아요.

phrases.en: The writer publishes a new novel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책을 내는 사람이나 회사 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요. '출판되다'와 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person or company that publishes. It pairs with 출판되다.

phrases.en: That book came out last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출판되다'와 비슷한 뜻인데, 책이 나왔다는 사실에 더 초점을 둬요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 출판되다 but focuses more on the fact that the book came out.

phrases.en: This book hasn't been published yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 책으로 나오지 않았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it hasn't come out as a book yet.

explain_en: A book gets printed and released — general (새 책이 출판돼요) In speech '책이 나왔어요' sounds more natural. '출판되다' is for printed matter like books and magazines. For things posted online, use '게시되다' or '올라오다'.

dis.h: a book gets printed and released
gh: a book comes out; common in publisher news

p.n: Almost the same; 출간 is a bit more literary.

t90.ax: This novel was published ten years ago.

en: to wriggle; to squirm; to crawl

examples.en: The puppies are wriggling in their mother's arms.
A caterpillar is squirming on a leaf.
The baby wriggled its hands and feet under the blanket.

examples.ko: 개미 몇 마리가 바닥에서 꼬물거리는 게 보여요.
examples.en: I can see a few ants wriggling on the floor.
The tadpoles wriggling in the water are so cute.
Every time the baby squirms, I can't help smiling.

explain: 작고 귀여운 것이 천천히 움직일 때 써서 아기, 강아지, 올챙이, 애벌레에 잘 어울려요. '꼬물대다'도 같은 뜻이고 부사는 '꼬물꼬물'이에요.

phrases.en: Tadpoles are wriggling in the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼬물거리다'와 같은 뜻이라 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 꼬물거리다, so they are interchangeable.

phrases.en: The baby is wriggling around under the blanket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '꼬물꼬물'을 붙여 움직이는 모습을 더 생생하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb 꼬물꼬물 makes the movement more vivid.

phrases.en: I saw a caterpillar wriggling on a leaf.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the '-는' form to modify a noun.

explain_en: Tiny creatures or babies moving slowly and softly — cute tone. It is used for small, cute things moving slowly, so it suits babies, puppies, tadpoles and caterpillars. '꼬물대다' means the same, and the adverb is '꼬물꼬물'.

t90.ax: A caterpillar is squirming on a leaf.

examples.en: Korea is a country short on water resources.
I use water sparingly to save water resources.
Managing water resources is an important job of the government.
When the climate changes, water resources change too.
A campaign to protect water resources was held.
I want to work at a water resources institute.

explain: '물'은 일상의 말이고 '수자원'은 사람이 쓸 수 있는 물을 나라나 지역 단위로 이야기할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '수자원 부족', '수자원 관리'처럼 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Each country has a different way of managing water resources.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in news and writing.

phrases.example: 이 지역은 수자원이 풍부해서 농사짓기 좋아요.
phrases.en: This area has abundant water resources, so it is good for farming.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부족하다'의 반대로 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of saying resources are lacking.

phrases.example: 우리는 강을 깨끗이 해서 수자원을 보호해야 해요.
phrases.en: We have to keep rivers clean to protect water resources.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in talk about the environment.

explain_en: 물 is the everyday word, while 수자원 is used for the water people can use, talked about at the level of a country or region. In the news it appears as '수자원 부족' (shortage) and '수자원 관리' (management).

examples.en: Water flowing downward is also a law of nature.
Scientists study the laws of nature.
No one can change the laws of nature.
This experiment proceeds according to the laws of nature.
That is as natural as a law of nature.

examples.ko: 자연법칙 덕분에 비행기가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the laws of nature, airplanes can fly.

explain: 중력처럼 늘 똑같이 작용하는 규칙을 말해서, 사람이 정하는 '법'이나 '규칙'과는 달라요. 일상 대화에서는 '당연한 이치'라는 뜻으로 비유해서 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The changing of seasons is a law of nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같고 일상 대화에서 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but sounds softer in everyday talk.

phrases.en: All objects move according to the laws of nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 설명에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often used in scientific explanations.

phrases.example: 나이가 들면 늙는 건 자연의 이치예요.
phrases.en: Growing old with age is the natural order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학보다는 삶의 당연한 흐름을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the natural course of life more than to science.

explain_en: It refers to rules like gravity that always work the same way, so it differs from '법' or '규칙' made by people. In daily talk it is also used figuratively to mean something that is only natural.

examples.en: Korea is a country without many underground resources.
Oil and coal are typical underground resources.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 지하자원을 수출해서 돈을 벌어요.
examples.en: That country earns money by exporting its underground resources.
If you dig up underground resources excessively, the environment gets damaged.
I envy countries rich in underground resources.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 지하자원 개발에 관한 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about developing underground resources on the news.

explain: 석유, 석탄, 철, 금처럼 땅속에서 나오는 자원을 한꺼번에 가리키는 말이에요. '풍부하다/부족하다', '개발하다/캐다'와 자주 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: That country is rich in underground resources.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자원이 많은 나라나 지역을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a country or region with plenty of resources.

phrases.en: Miners dig up underground resources in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅속에서 직접 꺼내는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to actually digging resources out of the ground.

phrases.en: The government decided to develop underground resources.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자원을 쓸 수 있게 하는 큰 사업에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for large projects that make resources usable.

explain_en: It is a collective term for resources from underground such as oil, coal, iron and gold. It often appears with '풍부하다/부족하다' (abundant/lacking) and '개발하다/캐다' (develop/dig).

examples.ko: 작은 실수를 간과하면 나중에 큰 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: If you overlook a small mistake, it becomes a big problem later.

examples.ko: 이 점은 절대 간과할 수 없어요.
examples.en: We absolutely cannot overlook this point.
People overlooked the importance of safety.

examples.ko: 중요한 사실을 간과한 채 결정하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You should not decide while overlooking an important fact.
Please do not overlook that problem.

examples.ko: 간과하기 쉬운 부분을 한 번 더 확인해요.
examples.en: We check once more the parts that are easy to overlook.

explain: '간과'는 대부분 '간과하다'로 써요. '간과할 수 없다', '간과하기 쉽다'처럼 '중요한데 보지 못하고 지나친다'는 느낌이에요. 말할 때는 '놓치다'가 더 쉽고, '간과하다'는 글·발표·뉴스에서 많이 써요.

phrases.en: You shouldn't overlook even small problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: '간과'는 보통 이 동사형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '간과' is usually used in this verb form.

phrases.en: The safety issue cannot be overlooked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요해서 그냥 넘길 수 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it's too important to ignore.

phrases.en: Small habits are easy to overlook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놓치기 쉬운 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for things that are easy to miss.

explain_en: '간과' is mostly used as the verb '간과하다', in patterns like '간과할 수 없다' and '간과하기 쉽다', meaning missing something that is actually important. '놓치다' is easier in speech; '간과하다' is common in writing, presentations, and news.

examples.en: Judging by the result, that choice was right.
In hindsight, that investment was a success.

examples.ko: 이미 끝난 일을 결과론으로 따지지 마세요.
examples.en: Please do not judge things that are over by their results.

examples.ko: 그건 결과론일 뿐이에요, 그때는 아무도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: That is just hindsight; nobody knew at the time.
The coach answered the hindsight criticism calmly.

examples.ko: 결과가 좋았다고 과정까지 좋았다는 건 결과론이에요.
examples.en: Saying the process was good just because the outcome was good is judging by results.

explain: 과정은 보지 않고 결과만 가지고 판단할 때 쓰는, 조금 비판하는 말투예요. '결과론적으로', '결과론적인 이야기'처럼 자주 쓰고, '지금 와서 하는 말이지만'과 비슷한 상황에 어울려요.

phrases.en: That's only talk based on the result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 알고 나서 하는 말이라고 지적할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out that it's said with hindsight.

phrases.en: Saying it was right because it succeeded is just judging by the outcome.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과만 보고 판단한다는 비판을 담아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries criticism of judging only by the outcome.

phrases.en: Judging by the result, that choice was right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 알고 나서 과거를 평가할 때 문장 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used at the start of a sentence to judge the past after knowing the result.
phrases.en_equiv: looking at it by the outcome

explain_en: It has a mildly critical tone for judging only by the outcome and ignoring the process. It is often used as '결과론적으로' or '결과론적인 이야기', in situations like saying 'it is easy to say now'.

en: necessity; the reason it ought to be

examples.ko: 이 정책이 꼭 필요한 당위성을 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: Please explain why this policy is necessary and justified.

examples.ko: 환경을 지켜야 한다는 당위성은 누구나 알아요.
examples.en: Everyone knows we ought to protect the environment.

examples.ko: 당위성만 말하지 말고 방법도 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Don't just talk about why we should; tell us how, too.
His argument lacks a sense of necessity.
Opinions were divided on whether the plan was justified.
The 'ought to' matters, but you also have to look at reality.

explain: '그렇게 해야 마땅하다'는 이유를 말할 때 토론이나 글에서 많이 써요. '필요성'은 필요한 이유이고, 당위성은 옳기 때문에 해야 한다는 쪽에 더 가까워요. 일상 대화보다는 논설이나 발표에서 들려요.

phrases.en: That argument has sufficient justification.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그렇게 해야 할 이유가 마땅하다고 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say there is good reason why something ought to be done.

phrases.en: He argued for the imperative of reform.
phrases.nuance_ko: 토론이나 연설에서 '꼭 해야 한다'고 내세울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in debates or speeches when insisting something must be done.

phrases.en: Let's talk about the need for this system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 이유를 말할 때 쓰고, 당위성보다 '옳아서 해야 한다'는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the reason something is needed; less of a moral 'ought' than 당위성.

explain_en: Moral or logical grounds that something ought to be done. It is used in debates and writing for the reason something ought to be done. '필요성' is the reason something is needed, while 당위성 leans toward doing it because it is right. You hear it more in essays and presentations than in daily talk.

examples.en: Our company's motto is honesty.

examples.ko: 제 인생 모토가 뭐냐고 선생님이 물었어요.
examples.en: The teacher asked what my life motto is.

examples.ko: 학교 모토를 벽에 크게 써 붙였어요.
examples.en: We wrote the school motto large and stuck it on the wall.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 손님이 먼저라는 모토로 장사해요.
examples.en: This shop does business with the motto customers come first.

examples.ko: 좋은 모토 하나가 하루를 바꿀 수도 있어요.
examples.en: One good motto can change your day.
I try to act in line with my motto.

explain: 개인이 마음에 새기는 말은 '좌우명'이 더 자연스럽고, 회사나 단체가 내세우는 말에는 모토를 써요. 슬로건은 광고나 캠페인에 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: My personal motto is 'a little every day.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인이 마음에 새기는 말은 '모토'보다 '좌우명'이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a personal guiding phrase, 좌우명 sounds more natural than 모토.

phrases.en: I take 'do your best' as my motto.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 말을 기준으로 삼는다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you adopt a phrase as your guiding principle.

phrases.en: Our team's motto is 'let's go together.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 단체가 내세우는 말은 '모토' 앞에 단체 이름을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the group's name before 모토 for a motto of a team or group.

explain_en: Loanword motto; casual, used for families, teams, brands (우리 가족의 모토) For a personal guiding phrase, '좌우명' is more natural, while 모토 is used for what a company or group stands for. A slogan is a phrase used in ads or campaigns.

en: to be sullen; to be sulky

examples.en: My younger brother is sulking because he couldn't have a snack.
Why have you been sulking like that since morning?

examples.ko: 친구가 뾰로통한 얼굴로 아무 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: My friend said nothing, with a sulky look on her face.

examples.ko: 장난감을 뺏기자 아이 표정이 금세 뾰로통해졌어요.
examples.en: When his toy was taken, the child's face quickly turned sulky.
My girlfriend sits there sulking and just looks out the window.
Even when she pouts she's so cute that I can't get angry.

explain: 화가 크게 난 것보다는 못마땅해서 말없이 입을 내밀고 있는 느낌이에요. 어린아이나 가까운 사람이 삐쳤을 때 많이 써요. '뽀로통하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is sitting with a sulky expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뾰로통하다'의 활용형으로, 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form describing the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The child answered in a sulky way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로, 말이나 행동의 모습을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describing how someone speaks or acts.

phrases.en: My friend is sulking and won't talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 다른 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An alternative form with the same meaning.

explain_en: Visibly pouting with displeasure written on the face; often childlike and cute rather than heavy. It describes being displeased and silently pouting rather than being truly furious. It is often used for children or close people who are in a huff. '뽀로통하다' is also used for the same meaning.

t90.ax: Why have you been sulking like that since morning?

examples.en: The agency stated that the celebrity dating rumor is groundless.
The story that I borrowed money is completely baseless.
It's baseless, so please don't worry.
The article was baseless, so we demanded a correction.
Only after it turned out to be baseless did I feel relieved.

examples.ko: 회사는 사실무근의 주장에 법적으로 대응하겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: The company said it would respond legally to the baseless claims.

explain: 소문이나 보도, 주장을 강하게 부인할 때 쓰는 말로, 뉴스에서 '사실무근이라고 부인했다'처럼 자주 나와요. 친구끼리는 '그런 거 아니야'처럼 말하는 편이에요.

phrases.en: After an investigation, the rumor turned out to be groundless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확인해 보니 근거가 없었다는 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to report that checking showed there was no basis.

phrases.en: The shop had a hard time because of a baseless rumor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸밀 때는 '의'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '의' when it modifies a noun.

phrases.en: He denied the article, saying it was groundless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 소문을 강하게 부정할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common news phrase for firmly denying a rumor.

explain_en: It is used to firmly deny rumors, reports, or claims, and appears in the news in lines like '사실무근이라고 부인했다'. Among friends people would rather say something like '그런 거 아니야'.

examples.en: After long effort, I achieved my dream.
To achieve your goal, you have to practice every day.

examples.ko: 그는 짧은 시간에 큰 성공을 성취했어요.
examples.en: He accomplished great success in a short time.

examples.ko: 작은 목표를 하나씩 성취하는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: It's important to achieve small goals one by one.
After you accomplish something, you feel really good.
I want to help students achieve things on their own.

explain: 성취하다는 노력해서 목표나 꿈을 끝내 이룰 때 써요. '이루다'와 비슷하지만 성취하다는 힘들게 노력한 끝에 얻은 결과라는 느낌이 더 강해요. '성취감'은 목표를 이뤘을 때의 뿌듯함이에요.

phrases.en: I want to study hard and achieve my dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성취하다보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, everyday word for the same idea.

phrases.example: 문제를 다 풀고 나니 성취감이 느껴져요.
phrases.en: After solving all the problems, I feel a sense of accomplishment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목표를 이뤘을 때의 뿌듯한 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The proud feeling you get after reaching a goal.

phrases.en: I haven't achieved my goal yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목표를 아직 이루지 못했을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for when a goal is not yet reached.

explain_en: 성취하다 is used when you finally reach a goal or dream through effort. It is close to '이루다', but 성취하다 stresses a result earned by hard work. '성취감' is the proud feeling you get after reaching a goal.
